info.title: AuthorizationManagementClient
info.description:
Privileged Access — end-user API surface for Privileged Access Management.

Provides two resource types under `Microsoft.Authorization`:
1. `privilegedResources` (GET-only collection) — a unified view of the
Azure resources you have privileged access to.
2. `privilegedResourceFavorites` (PUT/GET/DELETE) — your personal resource
favorites.

Both resource types are tenant-scoped: they are addressed at the tenant, not
under a subscription or resource group.

get.description:
List the calling user's favorites.

The caller's principal id is taken from the validated user token, never
from the request. There is no API surface for one user to list another
user's favorites — favorites are partitioned per caller.

Get one of the calling user's favorites by id.

Returns `404` if the calling user has not favorited this resource, even
if another user has.

parameters.name: favoriteId
parameters.description:
Favorite identifier — `base64url(lowercased Azure resource ID)`. Because
the derivation is deterministic, the client may compute it locally
from the resource id.

put.description:
Add (or re-add) a favorite for the calling user.

Idempotent: re-favoriting an already-favorited resource returns the
existing record with status `200 OK` rather than creating a duplicate;
a new favorite returns `201 Created`. The service validates that
`{favoriteId}` equals `base64url(lowercased(properties.resourceId))`
(`400 InvalidRequest` on mismatch) and that the caller has read
permission on the resource (`403 Forbidden` otherwise).

parameters.name: favoriteId
parameters.description:
Favorite identifier — `base64url(lowercased Azure resource ID)`. Because
the derivation is deterministic, the client may compute it locally
from the resource id.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: The favorite to create or update.

delete.description:
Remove the calling user's favorite.

Idempotent. Returns `200 OK` when an existing favorite was removed and
`204 No Content` when no matching favorite existed for the caller.

parameters.name: favoriteId
parameters.description:
Favorite identifier — `base64url(lowercased Azure resource ID)`. Because
the derivation is deterministic, the client may compute it locally
from the resource id.

get.description:
List the calling user's privileged Azure resources.

Returns the resources you have privileged access to, evaluated with your
own permissions — only resources you are authorized to see are included.

Pagination: server-driven via `maxpagesize` (advisory) + `nextLink`.
Clients follow `nextLink` verbatim — do not parse, mutate, or append
query parameters.

parameters.name: accessScope
parameters.description:
Controls whether the response is scoped to subscriptions the caller has
PIM assignments on, or expanded to all readable subscriptions. Allowed
values today: `pimOnly` (default — only subscriptions with PIM
assignments) and `allAccessible` (any subscription the caller can read).

Modeled as an extensible string so future scope expansions can be
added without a breaking change; clients should tolerate unknown values.

values.name: PimOnly
values.description: Scope the response to subscriptions the caller has PIM assignments on.

values.name: AllAccessible
values.description: Expand the response to all subscriptions the caller can read.

parameters.name: maxpagesize
parameters.description:
Advisory maximum page-size hint. The server may return fewer items than
`maxpagesize` and still include a `nextLink`. Server cap: 1000. Name
follows the standard Azure pagination convention (`maxpagesize`)
rather than the strict-maximum `$top` to signal the advisory semantics.

parameters.name: $filter
parameters.description:
OData `$filter` expression that selects resource rows. Flat, lowercase
`and` expression only — `or`, `not`, and grouping are rejected.
Supported predicates:

- `type` — `eq` or `in`, e.g.
`type eq 'microsoft.compute/virtualmachines'` or
`type in ('microsoft.compute/virtualmachines','microsoft.desktopvirtualization/hostpools')`.
Every value must be a supported primary resource type.
- `scope` — `eq` or `in`, using exact, case-insensitive ARM-ID
membership.
- `subscriptionId` — `eq`, `ne`, or `in`. It is an exact resource GUID,
so `contains` / `startswith` are rejected.
- `subscriptionName` — `eq`, `ne`, `contains`, or `startswith`. The
human-readable subscription display name (distinct from the
`subscriptionId` GUID).
- `resourceGroup` — `eq`, `ne`, `contains`, `startswith`, or `in`.
Matches by name across every subscription the caller can see; because
resource-group names are not globally unique, combine it with
`subscriptionId` to disambiguate.
- `tags.<key>` (dynamic) — `eq`, `ne`, `contains`, or `startswith`.
A tag predicate addresses a single key with dotted syntax
(e.g. `tags.environment eq 'prod'`); the whole remainder after
`tags.` is the key, matched case-insensitively. An empty key
(`tags.`) is rejected.
- `displayName` and `location` — `eq`, `ne`, and function-form
`startswith(field,'value')` / `contains(field,'value')`.
- Favorite state: `isFavorite eq|ne true|false` — accepted and
validated, but does not filter rows in this revision.
- Role assignment status:
`roles/any(r: r/assignmentStatus eq 'active'|'eligible')`.

The `in` membership operator is limited to `type`, `scope`,
`subscriptionId`, and `resourceGroup`; all other fields accept only the
infix (`eq` / `ne`) and function (`contains` / `startswith`) forms.
`endswith` is not supported. Values inside one `in` clause are
OR-composed and matched case-insensitively; separate clauses remain
AND-composed.

A role assignment status predicate selects resource rows that have at
least one matching role; it does not filter the contents of `roles`.
Every matching resource returns its complete roles collection.

parameters.name: $orderby
parameters.description:
Sort expression. Supported values: `displayName`, `displayName asc`, or
`displayName desc`. Ordering is applied to the complete filtered set
before pagination, with `scope` as the deterministic tie-breaker.
Invalid expressions return `400 InvalidOrderBy`.

parameters.name: $count
parameters.description:
When `true`, the response includes the full post-filter row count in the
optional `count` field — the cardinality of the complete filtered set
before the page slice. Absent or `false` omits `count`. Any other value
returns `400 InvalidCount`.

get.description:
List the connect-enablement related resources for a privileged resource.

Returns the resources you must additionally access to connect to the
privileged resource identified by `{privilegedResourceId}` — for example,
for a virtual machine: the NIC, NSG, public IP, and Bastion host.

Each entry is itself a projection (`RelatedResourceProjection`): the related
resource's own `projectionId` and `scope`, plus the `roles` you hold
(active or eligible) on that related resource. Clients drive activation
against those roles to enable connect. Resource properties themselves are
NOT returned — read them directly from the Azure Resource Manager REST APIs
at Connect time.

Returns an empty page when the privileged resource has no connect-enablement
dependencies.

parameters.name: privilegedResourceId
parameters.description:
Opaque projection identifier of the parent privileged resource — the
`projectionId` returned by the `privilegedResources` list operation.
Clients MUST treat this as opaque — do not parse.

AssignmentStatus.description:
Status of a role assignment from the caller's perspective. Used by
`RoleAssignmentSummary.assignmentStatus` and by role status predicates in
the `PrivilegedResources.list` `$filter` expression.

Extensible string union — additional statuses can be added without a
breaking change; clients should tolerate unknown values.

values.name: Active
values.description: The user effectively has this role active right now.

values.name: Eligible
values.description:
The user can activate this role (one-step or two-step activation,
depending on the source's membership state).

GroupMembershipState.description:
User membership state in a group, used to discriminate one-step vs two-step
activation flows for group-sourced roles.

values.name: Active
values.description: The user is an active member of the group.

values.name: Eligible
values.description:
The user is an eligible member of the group — group membership must be
activated first before the inherited role can be activated.

GroupReference.description: A reference to a Microsoft Entra ID group through which a role is granted.

id.description: Microsoft Entra ID object id of the group.

GroupRoleSource.description:
Group-sourced role assignment. The role is granted via `group`;
the user's membership state in that group is recorded in `membershipState`.

group.description: The group through which this role is granted.

membershipState.description:
The user's membership state in the group. Drives client activation routing:

- `active`   → one-step (activate the role).
- `eligible` → two-step (activate your group membership first, then
activate the role).

MemberType.description:
Membership type of a role grant. Extensible union — clients SHOULD treat
unknown values as "unsupported membership type".

values.name: Group
values.description: Role granted via a group the user is a member of.

value.description: The PrivilegedResourceFavorite items on this page

nextLink.description: The link to the next page of items

value.description: The RelatedResourceProjection items on this page

nextLink.description: The link to the next page of items

PagedResourceProjection.description:
Paging envelope for the `privilegedResources` list operation.

Spreads the standard `Azure.Core.Page<ResourceProjection>` shape (`value` +
`nextLink`) and adds the optional `count` field. The envelope itself is not
an ARM resource — the ARM resource invariants are enforced on the page's
items (`ResourceProjection`), not on the wrapper.

value.description: The ResourceProjection items on this page

nextLink.description: The link to the next page of items

ParentResource.description:
Scope ancestor entry. Navigation only — carries no access information.

Generic shape: `type` classifies the scope tier; scope-type-specific metadata
lives inside the open `properties` bag and is mirrored from the upstream
scope without validation. Recursive: each entry has its own
`parentResource` pointing at the next scope up. Present on every entry
except the outermost (root) scope.

type.description:
Scope tier classification. Allowed values today: `resourceGroup`,
`subscription`. Future tiers (e.g., `managementGroup`, `tenant`, future
sub-resource hierarchies) are non-breaking additions — the `properties`
bag carries their per-type metadata.

scope.description:
Scope identifier for the parent scope. For Azure Resource Manager-addressable
scopes this is the full Azure Resource Manager resource path (e.g.,
`/subscriptions/{subId}/resourceGroups/my-rg`). Typed as `string` (not
`armResourceIdentifier`) because higher scope tiers — management groups,
tenants, and future non–Azure Resource Manager hierarchies — do not have
Azure Resource Manager resource identifiers. Format is determined by the
sibling `type` value.

displayName.description:
Human-readable scope name. For subscriptions, may be the subscription id
when a display name is unavailable.

properties.description:
Scope-type-specific metadata bag, mirrored from the upstream Azure scope
for the given `type`, without validation. The set of fields inside is
determined by the sibling `type` value. Always emitted (possibly empty
`{}`) so clients can safely read it. Intentionally untyped at the API
contract layer so new scope tiers (`managementGroup`, `tenant`, future
sub-resource hierarchies) can be added without a contract break.

Examples today (informative, not enforced by schema):

- `type = "resourceGroup"`: `{}` (no scope-specific metadata in v1).
- `type = "subscription"`:  `{ managementGroupPath: string[] }`
(ordered root-to-direct-parent).

Clients SHOULD treat the bag as opaque unless they know the `type`.

parentResource.description:
The next ancestor in the chain. Present on every entry except the
outermost (root) scope, which omits the field.

PrivilegedResourceFavorite.description:
A per-user resource favorite. Each user's favorites are private to them:
two different users issuing PUT against the same `{favoriteId}` create two
independent favorite records.

Operations (defined in routes.tsp):
- LIST   `GET    /providers/Microsoft.Authorization/privilegedResourceFavorites`
- GET    `GET    /providers/Microsoft.Authorization/privilegedResourceFavorites/{favoriteId}`
- PUT    `PUT    /providers/Microsoft.Authorization/privilegedResourceFavorites/{favoriteId}` (idempotent)
- DELETE `DELETE /providers/Microsoft.Authorization/privilegedResourceFavorites/{favoriteId}` (idempotent)

`{favoriteId}` is deterministically derived from the favorited Azure resource
path: `favoriteId = base64url(lowercased Azure resource ID)`. Because the
derivation is deterministic, the client may compute the id locally and
issue the PUT/GET/DELETE without an additional round-trip; the service
validates the derivation on PUT.

Favorites are not scoped to any subscription or resource group — they belong
to the calling user.

properties.description: The resource-specific properties for this resource.

PrivilegedResourceFavoriteProperties.description:
Properties of a `PrivilegedResourceFavorite`. The favorite's identity
(`favoriteId` / `name`) is the URL-segment derivation of `resourceId`:
`favoriteId = base64url(lowercased Azure resource ID)`.

Favorites are created synchronously — a successful PUT or DELETE takes effect
immediately, with no long-running operation to poll.

resourceId.description:
The favorited Azure resource id. The `favoriteId` URL segment MUST equal
`base64url(lowercased(resourceId))`; the service rejects mismatches with
`400 InvalidRequest` on PUT.

Effectively immutable: set on create and never changed afterward — there is
no PATCH, and PUT validates the `favoriteId`-from-`resourceId` derivation.

RelatedResourceProjection.description:
A connect-enablement resource for a privileged resource — an Azure resource
the caller must be able to access to connect to the primary resource (for a
virtual machine, typically the NIC, NSG, public IP, or Bastion host),
projected with its own scope and the roles the caller holds on it.

projectionId.description:
Opaque server-generated identifier for this related-resource projection.
Stable per (caller, related resource) pair. Clients MUST treat this as
opaque — do not parse.

scope.description:
Fully-qualified Azure resource path of the related (connect-enablement)
resource — e.g. the virtual machine's NIC, NSG, public IP, or Bastion host.

As with `ResourceProjection.scope`, every resource is also a scope at which
role assignments can be granted, so this field uses the ARM-standard
`scope` name.

roles.description:
Every role granting the caller access to this related resource — direct or
inherited, direct-source or group-source, active or eligible. Each entry's
`scope` field records the actual assignment scope. The caller activates the
appropriate role here to enable connect to the primary resource.

ResourceProjection.description:
A privileged resource projection — a unified view of an Azure resource the
caller has privileged access to, with all role information flattened onto the
row. Connect-enablement dependencies are retrieved separately via
`GET .../privilegedResources/{privilegedResourceId}/relatedResources`.

The Azure resource-type namespace (`type`, e.g.
`microsoft.compute/virtualmachines`) is the discriminator — new resource
types are non-breaking additions and clients SHOULD tolerate unknown
values.

projectionId.description:
Opaque server-generated identifier for this projection row. Stable per
(caller, resource) pair. Clients MUST treat this as opaque — do not parse.

Distinct from the conventional Azure resource `id`: the full Azure
resource path lives on `scope` below.

scope.description:
Fully-qualified Azure resource path (e.g.,
`/subscriptions/{subId}/resourceGroups/my-rg/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/my-vm`).

In the privileged-access model every resource is also a scope at which
role assignments can be granted, so this field uses the ARM-standard
`scope` name rather than `resourceId`.

type.description:
Azure resource provider type (lowercased), e.g.
`microsoft.compute/virtualmachines`. This is the ARM-standard `type`
field and also serves as the resource-kind discriminator — new resource
types are non-breaking additions.

tags.description:
Azure resource tags, mirrored verbatim from the upstream Azure resource.
Free-form user-defined key/value pairs, not validated — identical semantics
to standard Azure Resource Manager `TrackedResource.tags`.

parentResource.description:
Scope ancestor chain — innermost (resource group) first, outermost
(subscription, future management group) at the chain's tail. Navigation
only; carries no access information.

Inheritance of role assignments is recorded directly on each entry of
`roles` (each role's `scope` field), not by walking this chain. Clients
do not need to walk `parentResource` to discover inherited roles.

roles.description:
Every role granting access to this resource — direct or inherited from
any ancestor scope, and direct or via group membership (active or eligible).
Each entry's `scope` field records the actual assignment scope.

Inherited and group-sourced roles are already included and fully resolved
here: clients do NOT need to walk `parentResource` or resolve group
membership themselves.

isFavorite.description:
Whether you have favorited this resource (see
`privilegedResourceFavorites`). Always populated on every row.

RoleAssignmentSummary.description:
A single role grant on the resource. Roles for a row are flattened: direct
and inherited assignments, direct-source and group-source assignments
(whether active or eligible), all appear as separate entries with their
actual assignment scope recorded in `scope`. The same role at the same
scope from the same source MUST NOT appear twice on the same row.

roleId.description:
Opaque, stable identifier for this role grant. Stable per assignment, so it
is safe to use as a client-side collection key. Clients MUST treat this as
opaque — do not parse.

parentRoleId.description: The identifier of the parent role, if this role has a parent.

roleDisplayName.description:
Human-readable display name of the role definition (e.g.
`Network Contributor`). Provided as a convenience so clients can render the
role without a separate lookup on `roleDefinitionId`.

scope.description:
Azure scope path where the assignment is granted (resource, resource
group, subscription, or future management-group id). Inheritance is
implicit: if `scope` differs from the row's `scope` (the resource's
own path), the role is inherited.

assignmentStatus.description:
The caller's current status against this role on this resource:

- `active`   — the user effectively has this role active right now.
- `eligible` — the user can activate this role (one-step or two-step
activation, depending on `source.membershipState`).

Modeled as an extensible string so future statuses (e.g. additional
lifecycle states) can be added without a breaking change; clients should
tolerate unknown values.

scheduleInfo.description:
Schedule (start time and expiration) backing this role grant. Populated for
both `active` and `eligible` entries. A permanent (no-expiry) assignment is
represented by `expiration.type` = `NoExpiration`; a time-bound assignment
by `AfterDuration` (with `duration`) or `AfterDateTime` (with `endDateTime`).

source.description: Origin of the role grant — direct user assignment or via group membership.

isLeastPrivilege.description:
Whether this role is a least-privilege role for the resource. A value of
`true` indicates the role grants the minimum permissions needed and is the
recommended choice; `false` indicates a broader-privilege role. Provided as
a recommendation so clients can guide users toward the least-privilege
option.

RoleSource.description: Origin of a role grant. Discriminated by `memberType`.

memberType.description:
Membership type: `direct` (direct user assignment) or `group` (granted via
a group the user is a member of).

ScheduleExpiration.description: Expiration of a role grant schedule.

type.description:
Type of expiration: `AfterDuration` (time-bound by `duration`),
`AfterDateTime` (time-bound by `endDateTime`), or `NoExpiration`
(permanent).

endDateTime.description: End DateTime of the schedule. Set when `type` is `AfterDateTime`.

duration.description:
Duration of the schedule as an ISO-8601 TimeSpan. Set when `type` is
`AfterDuration`.

ScheduleExpirationType.description: Expiration kind of a role grant schedule. Extensible string union.

values.name: AfterDuration
values.description: Time-bound assignment expiring after a duration — `duration` is set.

values.name: AfterDateTime
values.description:
Time-bound assignment expiring at an explicit end date — `endDateTime` is
set.

ScheduleInfo.description: Schedule info backing a role grant — start time and expiration.

expiration.description: Expiration of the schedule. Absent implies no expiration is expressed.

ScopeKind.description:
Scope-tier classification for `ParentResource`. Extensible union — `type`
is a classification tag (NOT a strict schema discriminator); per-type
metadata lives in the `properties` bag.
